system_message:
You are an expert software requirements analyst with deep knowledge of:
- Software development lifecycle (SDLC)
- User story analysis
- Acceptance criteria decomposition
- Edge case identification
- Test-driven development

YOUR TASK:
Analyze the provided user story/ticket and extract structured requirements.

EXTRACT:
1. Functional Requirements - What the system should DO
2. Technical Requirements - HOW to implement (specific code changes, APIs, components)
3. Edge Cases - Error scenarios, boundary conditions, unexpected inputs
4. Acceptance Tests - Test cases to verify functionality
5. Affected Components - Which modules/files will change  5. Affected Components - Which modules/files will change
  6. Non-Functional Requirements - Performance, security, scalability needs
  7. Risk - (low, medium, high)
  8. Complexity - (low, medium, high)
  9. Ticket Category - (Feature, Bug, Config, Refactor)
  10. Expected Files - Specific file paths expected
  11. Estimated Work - (small, medium, large)


RULES:
- Be SPECIFIC - avoid vague requirements like "improve performance"
- Include file paths if mentioned (e.g., "Update src/components/CheckoutForm.tsx")
- Extract ALL edge cases mentioned or implied
- Generate testable acceptance criteria
- Identify ALL affected components

RESPOND with JSON ONLY using this exact structure:
{
  "functional_requirements": ["Req 1", "Req 2"],
  "technical_requirements": ["Tech req 1", "Tech req 2"],
  "edge_cases": ["Edge case 1", "Edge case 2"],
  "acceptance_tests": ["Test 1", "Test 2"],
  "affected_components": ["Component 1", "Component 2"],
  "non_functional_requirements": ["NFR 1", "NFR 2"]
}

NO markdown, NO explanations, ONLY JSON.
user_message:
TICKET ID: 4157705
TITLE: Core for Supplier Exchange - Make user email address case insensitive
PRIORITY: High

DESCRIPTION:
API currently treats email case as sensitive and returns 400 for different casing. Fix server-side behavior.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Email comparison is case-insensitive
- Existing behavior unchanged for valid users

LABELS: backend, api, bug

Now extract structured requirements in JSON format.

ticket.title: Core for Supplier Exchange - Make user email address case insensitive
ticket.description: API currently treats email case as sensitive and returns 400 for different casing. Fix server-side behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Existing behavior unchanged for valid users

investigation.root_cause_hypothesis: The email address comparison logic in the API is currently case-sensitive, leading to incorrect 400 responses when the casing differs.
possible_causes: Direct string comparison of email addresses without case normalization.
Database schema might be case-sensitive for email fields, requiring application-level normalization before comparison.
investigation.explanation: The ticket explicitly states that the API 'currently treats email case as sensitive and returns 400 for different casing', which is a clear description of a bug. The acceptance criteria also confirm the desired behavior is case-insensitive comparison. Therefore, it's a bug fix requiring code changes.
investigation.recommended_action: Modify the API's server-side logic to perform case-insensitive comparisons for user email addresses. This likely involves converting email addresses to a consistent case (e.g., lowercase) before comparison.

functional_requirements: The API shall perform case-insensitive comparisons for user email addresses.
The API shall not change existing behavior for valid users when email comparison is performed.
technical_requirements: Modify the server-side logic that handles user email validation and lookup to convert email addresses to a consistent case (e.g., lowercase) before comparison.
Ensure that the database query or comparison mechanism for user emails is updated to be case-insensitive.
edge_cases: User attempts to log in with an email address that differs only in casing from their registered email.
User attempts to register with an email address that differs only in casing from an already registered email.
API endpoint receives an email address with mixed casing (e.g., 'TestUser@Example.com').
API endpoint receives an email address with all uppercase or all lowercase characters.
acceptance_tests: Given a user is registered with 'TestUser@Example.com', when the user attempts to log in with 'testuser@example.com', then the login should be successful and a 200 OK response should be returned.
Given a user is registered with 'TestUser@Example.com', when the user attempts to log in with 'TESTUSER@EXAMPLE.COM', then the login should be successful and a 200 OK response should be returned.
Given no user is registered with 'NewUser@Example.com', when a new user attempts to register with 'newuser@example.com', then the registration should be successful.
Given no user is registered with 'NewUser@Example.com', when a new user attempts to register with 'NEWUSER@EXAMPLE.COM', then the registration should be successful.
Given a user is registered with 'TestUser@Example.com', when an API call is made to retrieve user details using 'testuser@example.com', then the correct user details should be returned.
Given a user is registered with 'TestUser@Example.com', when an API call is made to retrieve user details using 'TESTUSER@EXAMPLE.COM', then the correct user details should be returned.
affected_components: Database interaction layer for user data
non_functional_requirements: The change should not introduce any performance degradation in user authentication or registration processes.
The solution should maintain the security of user credentials and data.
